answers.responseText: Abstracting the two MEM cells gives a four-state FSM (one state per pair of stored bits). Building the state table by tracing each input through both half-adder stages and converting it to a diagram shows the machine adds a fixed constant to its binary input stream, carrying between steps.

Tracing machine B, the two NOTs cancel and the MEM delays the input one step, so B outputs its input shifted one tick: 2x in binary. Abstracting machine A’s MEM in the same way yields a state graph with the same transitions and outputs, so the two SCs implement the same FSM even though their circuitry differs — multiple realizability.
